clue.text: Conflict over the water takes inexperienced medic west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the whole run is turned backwards

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
doc is short for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A war at sea is joined by a green young doctor heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west' turns the whole run RAWDOC backwards. The Cod Wars were fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland in the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing-rights dispute fought between navies and trawlers at sea, so a conflict over the water.

clue.text: Devise new tin cover

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone thinks up a new lid for a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective on the cover; it is the anagram signal on TINCOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise is to invent or engineer a plan, a synonym.

clue.text: Show contempt for god of the underworld

definitions.meaning: to disrespect or insult someone, informal slang
The Roman god of the dead, Pluto

explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for insulting someone, and the Roman ruler of the dead in Latin myth.

clue.text: Philosopher disturbing to realist

indicators.note: disturbing means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A thinker unsettles someone who prides themselves on being a realist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbing' rearranges the letters of TOREALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker who taught Alexander the Great is the archetypal philosopher.

clue.text: Polished debate in outbuilding

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a shed is a garden outbuilding
a moot is a debate, as in a moot court or a moot point

explanation.surface: An argument is polished up in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished and made even are synonyms, as of a surface rubbed flat.

clue.text: In religious campaign maiden is against wickedness, imbued with love

indicators.note: against means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written

indicators.note: imbued with means filled with, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: sin is wickedness
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman on a crusade stands against wickedness, filled with love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbued with' puts O inside SIN to make SION; 'against' sets M and IS beside it. M for maiden is a cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is an evangelising campaign by a church, a synonym.

clue.text: Start being performed on TV?

parts.note: a show being performed is on
a television is a TV set

explanation.surface: A programme begins as it is broadcast on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of something, especially an illness, is its start.

clue.text: Divine food in shed overlooking river — something everyone will share

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking means sitting above, so the river comes after
in means the food is placed within the shed

parts.note: a hut is a shed
manna is the food sent from heaven in Exodus
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Heavenly food kept in a shed above the river is something everyone shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'overlooking' places the shed-and-food block above the river in this down entry. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The traits common to all people are by definition shared by everyone.

clue.text: One who writes a cheque for artist …

definitions.meaning: the person who signs a cheque is its ... in banking terms

explanation.definitionFit: Banking term for the signer of a cheque, and literally one who draws pictures.

clue.text: … Turning up here for prize

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: after the ellipsis, here points to the previous answer, the artist who draws

explanation.surface: Continuing the cheque story, money turns up here as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the clue before: 'here' is that answer, DRAWER, and 'Turning up' reverses it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given for an achievement, a synonym.

clue.text: Numbers gathered around a street start to spread hostility

indicators.note: gathered around means the numbers enclose the other letters

parts.note: nines are numbers

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Figures gather round a road and the hostility starts to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered around' makes the numbers enclose 'a street'; 'start to' takes the first letter of spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and ill will make up nastiness, a near synonym.

clue.text: Peaceful army capturing a second group of islands

indicators.note: capturing means one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, an army that does not fight
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A pacifist force takes a group of islands in a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' has the army enclose 'a second'. The Salvation Army is a Christian charity organised on military lines, hence peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is a South Pacific archipelago, an example of an island group.

clue.text: A hundred books educated woman has got about cheese

indicators.note: about means the woman's name goes round the other letters

parts.note: Rita is the heroine of Willy Russell's play Educating Rita
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A learned woman with a hundred books has got some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the woman's name go round the hundred and the books. She is the heroine of Willy Russell's play Educating Rita.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese, an example.

clue.text: Pass over place that could be "beauty spot"

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a location is a place

explanation.surface: Walkers cross a mountain pass towards a scenic beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets COL above LOCATION in the down entry. The definition is by example: beauty spot is a fixed word pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists call a habitual word pairing, such as beauty with spot, a fixed combination of this kind.

clue.text: In pain ten seem feverish

indicators.note: In signals that the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone in pain looks feverish ten times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters running across 'pain ten seem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is frantic and intense, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Invalid with a nature that's troubled?

definitions.text: Invalid with a nature that's troubled?

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An invalid whose temperament is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges INVALID and ANATURE together; the whole clue also describes the answer, a hypochondriac.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sickly person anxious about their health, which is exactly an invalid with a troubled nature.

clue.text: Always turning up drinking wine, one must be able not to leak it maybe!

definitions.text: able not to leak it maybe!

indicators.note: drinking means the reversed word takes the others inside it
in a down clue turning up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always
tent is a Spanish red wine used in communion
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps drinking wine must hold their water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives REVE in this down entry; 'drinking' puts the wine and one inside it. Tent is a dark Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being able to hold in, like a sealed container or a good memory, is to be retaining.

clue.text: Mad man aboard ship falls apart

indicators.note: aboard means one thing is carried inside a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the Mad Hatter is the character from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A lunatic on board ship causes everything to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts the madman inside the ship; the Mad Hatter is the character from Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To break into pieces is to disintegrate, a synonym for falling apart.

clue.text: It was supposedly Washington's aim, frankly

definitions.meaning: in the cherry-tree legend young George Washington said he could not lie

explanation.definitionFit: The legend says Washington could never lie, and the phrase is also an idiom meaning candidly.

clue.text: Constant amount of illumination?

definitions.meaning: Constant ... was an English composer and conductor
a unit of luminance in physics

explanation.definitionFit: First name and surname of an English composer, and a physics unit of brightness.

clue.text: Hired murderer decapitated us poet

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: Walt Whitman is the American poet of Leaves of Grass

explanation.surface: A contract killer beheads an American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the W from WHITMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is slang for a contract killer paid to murder.

clue.text: Ponder with hesitation in a building full of old stuff?

definitions.text: a building full of old stuff?

parts.note: to muse is to ponder
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone stands musing and hesitating in a building full of antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallery housing historic artefacts is jokingly a building full of old stuff.

clue.text: University's original active element?

parts.note: the first letter of University is the chemical symbol, and this metal was where radioactivity was first discovered

explanation.surface: The college's first active ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: U, the first letter of University, is this metal's chemical symbol; Becquerel discovered radioactivity in its salts, so it is the original active element.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy metal with symbol U was the first substance found to be radioactive.

clue.text: What this person does sometimes in a card game sets a pattern

parts.note: this person is the setter speaking, I

parts.words: does sometimes in a card game
parts.note: a card player sometimes deals the cards

explanation.surface: The dealer at the card table sets the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'What I do sometimes at cards': I + DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model to copy is a pattern or exemplar, a synonym.

clue.text: Line established by a new chap after the end of revolt

indicators.note: after means these pieces follow the letter taken from revolt
the end of means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A new man takes the line after the revolt ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes the T of revolt; 'after' puts A, N and GENT behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: Thrown into river is the Italian outcast

indicators.note: thrown into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian outcast is thrown into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown into' puts the Italian article inside the river, the Exe in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone banished from their country, an outcast.

clue.text: Dispose of tea possibly having drunk a cider earlier

indicators.note: earlier means this rearranged cider comes before the tea
drunk means these letters are reeling into a new order
possibly means the word tea is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of their tea after drinking a cider first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ACIDER to ERADIC; 'possibly' rearranges TEA to ATE; 'earlier' puts the cider part first.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely is to get rid of, a synonym.

clue.text: Wild animal in a gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym at school

explanation.surface: A wild beast is loose in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla or chimpanzee is an ape, an example of a wild animal.

clue.text: Big pillar I look around in August maybe

indicators.note: in means the short pieces go inside the month

parts.note: August is an example of a month

indicators.note: around means the words I and look are together turned backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone gazes round a huge column during the summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns 'I look' backwards, making OLI, which 'in' places inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A single huge standing block of stone is a big pillar.

clue.text: Apse in church with saints about to be given pride of place

indicators.text: to be given pride of place
indicators.note: pride of place means put at the front, so this word leads

parts.note: re means about, concerning
CE is the Church of England
S is short for saint, so SS is saints

explanation.surface: In the church's apse, saints are given the place of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be given pride of place' puts RE first, ahead of CE and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a recessed alcove at the end of a church, so a recess.
